title: Demo deck and report specs are valid
scenario: The shipped demo deck (10 slides, 5 sources) and report (4 sections).
expected: Both pass the spec check.

title: Unknown slide layout refused
scenario: A slide with layout 'nope'.
expected: SpecError naming the allowed layouts.

title: Citation of a source that is not listed refused
scenario: A bullet cites [S9] with no S9 in sources.
expected: SpecError: not listed (no dangling citation reaches the deck).

title: javascript: source link refused
scenario: A source URL 'javascript:alert(1)'.
expected: SpecError: only http(s) links.

title: Chart values that do not match labels refused
scenario: A chart with 1 label and 2 values.
expected: SpecError before building.

title: A stats slide with more than 4 items is refused, not silently cut
scenario: A 'stats' slide with 6 items (the layout has 4 cards).
expected: SpecError explaining the limit.

title: Deck builds without external tools, all text fits, file intact
scenario: Build the demo deck with python-pptx only.
expected: 11 slides (10 + sources), every text box fits, zip integrity OK, native charts present, under 10 s.

title: Source links are clickable and notes are written
scenario: The built demo deck.
expected: Every source URL is a hyperlink relationship; speaker-notes parts exist.

title: Too much text is reported, never silently clipped
scenario: A bullets slide with 12 sixty-word bullets.
expected: Refused by the spec check or reported as not fitting by the build.

title: Report HTML escapes script and event handlers
scenario: A paragraph containing <script> and an onerror attribute.
expected: Escaped text; no executable markup in the report.

title: Citations in the report link to the source list
scenario: The demo report.
expected: Citation markers are links to the sources section.

title: Report prints to PDF with nothing off the page and QA passes (Chrome stand-in)
scenario: The demo report HTML printed by headless Chrome (same engine as Edge).
expected: No words outside the page area; check_report passes.

title: Only made files can be opened; path tricks refused
scenario: Paths with '..', absolute system files, and a .exe inside the output folder.
expected: All refused; the tool's own PDF accepted; job folder under the output root with a safe name.

title: Same title never overwrites an earlier deliverable
scenario: Three jobs with the same title in the same second.
expected: Three distinct folders.

title: Missing Microsoft Edge is said plainly
scenario: Printing a report on a machine without Edge.
expected: ToolError naming Edge, no install command from a third party.

title: Missing OfficeCLI: animation is not claimed
scenario: Animating a deck when OfficeCLI is absent.
expected: ToolError; no success reported.

title: PDF printed by the laptop's Microsoft Edge
scenario: Edge prints the report with headers/footers.
expected: Laptop check.

title: Animations validated by OfficeCLI and shown in PowerPoint
scenario: OfficeCLI adds transitions/entrances; PowerPoint slideshow starts.
expected: Laptop check.

title: Wrongly typed spec fields are refused, not crashed on
scenario: Deck specs with layout 5, bullet level 'high', chart type 3; report specs with section kind 3 and bullet level 'x' (a model's malformed tool arguments).
expected: Each is refused with SpecError (the error the plugin entry reports), never AttributeError/ValueError.

title: Non-finite chart numbers are refused before building
scenario: Chart values 'nan', 'inf', 1e309 and '-inf'.
expected: Each is refused with SpecError before any file is made.

title: Control characters from extracted text never show on slides
scenario: A slide title, bullets and notes with vertical tab, form feed, NUL, bell and SOH characters (as text copied out of documents carries).
expected: The deck builds and reopens with python-pptx; no '_x00NN_' code appears in any slide text or note; the words are kept.

title: Report HTML keeps only web links and loads nothing remote
scenario: Untrusted report text with markdown links to javascript:, file:, data:, vbscript:, an image at http://127.0.0.1 and a tracker image in a callout.
expected: Every href is http(s) or in-page (#); no img/iframe/script/link/object/embed loads from another address (the HTML is saved next to the PDF and can be opened).

title: Printing a report makes no network request
scenario: A report whose text embeds an image and a link to a local server is printed (JS off, all requests blocked; Chrome stands in for Edge).
expected: The PDF is made and the local server receives no request.

title: Markup in report fields cannot break out of attributes
scenario: A source URL with '" onmouseover="alert(1)', a title with
expected: Parsed with lxml, the report HTML has no on* attribute and no script, iframe or img element.

title: The page footer prints the title as text
scenario: Report title 'Plan bold ' printed (Chrome stand-in for Edge).
expected: The last page's text contains 'bold' and '' literally (escaped, not markup).

title: Links out of the outputs folder cannot be opened
scenario: Inside a deliverable folder: report.pdf is a symlink to a file outside, and 'more' is a symlink to an outside folder.
expected: inside_outputs refuses both.

title: Regenerate only from a deliverable folder
scenario: regenerate() on a folder outside the outputs root holding a spec.json, and on a symlinked folder inside the root pointing outside (report maker replaced by a fake that counts builds).
expected: Both are refused with ToolError; nothing is built.

title: QA reports text drawn off the page
scenario: Two PDFs made with matplotlib: one with a word placed beyond the right page edge, one clean.
expected: words_off_page reports 'OVERFLOW' for the first and nothing for the clean one.

title: QA on a damaged PDF says 'not passed'
scenario: check_report on a PDF cut in half and on random bytes behind a %PDF header.
expected: Each result is 'not passed' with a reason; never 'passed' and never a raw parser exception.

title: Only the listed sources become deck hyperlinks
scenario: Bullets and notes carry a markdown javascript: link, an HTML anchor to file:///etc/passwd and a bare phishing URL.
expected: The built .pptx's external link targets are a non-empty subset of the spec's source URLs.

title: A research report becomes a valid deck that keeps its citations
scenario: research core.to_deck on a checked report with a 453-character summary statement and long section statements ending in [S1][S2].
expected: deliverables spec.deck accepts the deck spec; long statements are cut (at least two) and every cut statement keeps both citation markers.

title: Simultaneous deliverables with the same title get their own folders
scenario: Five rounds of eight threads calling new_job_dir('Same title') at the same moment.
expected: No error and 40 distinct folders.

title: The largest allowed deck builds in time
scenario: 40 bullet slides of 12 points each, with notes (the spec's maximum).
expected: At least the 40 content slides are built (the builder adds its own), the .pptx is intact, text fit is reported for every built slide, in under 60 s on one CPU.
